newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips after EU grain auction.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips after EU grain auction.

text.p: French wheat prices slipped Thursday after European Union granted lower wheat tonnages and export rebates than some operators had hoped, dealers said.

Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 855 francs for December delivery and at 840 francs for January delivery, both down five francs from levels reached before reports on the outcome of the grain auction hit the market.
EU granted 198,900 tonnes EU free-market soft wheat at a rebate of 18.000 Ecus per tonne.
"That is less than 200,000 tonnes and that is really not enough," a dealer said.
EU must maintain a weekly wheat export pace of at least 300,000 tonnes to export its bumper crop this season and avoid large sales into intervention stores, traders estimate.
In a move to provide relief to hard-pressed African nations, EU also set a special refund of 28 Ecus a tonne for wheat exports to a target group of African nations.
Dealers called the measure "interesting," adding a 28 Ecus rebate applying to wheat exports to all non-EU countries would be needed to allow the EU to make a headway into world markets.
